candidates: In workflow companion documentation files (e.g., `.github/workflows/*.md`), proofread both prose text for typos—especially in placeholder variables like branch or version name templates—and verify that every referenced job name matches the actual `jobs.<id>` key in the corresponding `.yml` file before merging.

In `workflow_dispatch` workflows that accept a PR number as input and check out that PR's code, add an explicit fail-fast step immediately after retrieving PR metadata that exits with a non-zero status when the PR is from a fork (`isCrossRepository == true`). This step must appear before any step that accesses secrets or publishes to a registry, because the admin-actor permission check only guards who triggers the workflow, not which code is executed.

When a workflow job checks out code from an external PR or fork (using a dynamic `repository`/`ref` in `actions/checkout`), do not reference local composite actions (`./.github/actions/…`) from that checked-out code. The action definition will resolve to the fork's copy rather than the repository's own copy. Either inline the steps or perform an additional checkout of the base repository's actions before using them.

In `actions/cache@v4` configurations, do not include an entry in `restore-keys` that is identical to the primary `key`. Restore-keys are only consulted when the primary key produces a cache miss, so a duplicate entry is dead code that serves no purpose and misleads readers about the fallback logic.

Every step that runs `yarn release:publish` must include `YARN_NPM_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}` (or the project's canonical NPM auth secret) in its `env` block. Omitting this causes the publish command to fail authentication against the npm registry silently.

Before merging any workflow change, verify that every `steps.<id>.outputs.<name>` reference in a job has a step with that exact `id` defined earlier in the same job. A dangling reference always evaluates as falsy at runtime and can silently produce wrong behavior (e.g., wrong Sentry environment, wrong release tag). Use actionlint in CI to catch these as compile-time errors.
